text.p: Atlantis Communications Corp said on Friday it began production of 22 new one-hour episodes of its award-winning "Traders" television show.
The Toronto-based TV producer -- which also makes "The Outer Limits" -- said the episodes would begin airing in Canada in September and had been presold in 20 countries.
A company official told Reuters that for its third season "Traders" would have a budget of between C$800,000 (US$580,000) and C$1 million (US$723,000) per episode.

A critical hit in Canada, "Traders" is set at a brokerage firm in Toronto's financial district. The drama was carried during its first two 13-episode seasons on the CanWest Global network, owned by CanWest Global Communications Inc.

Atlantis said in April that for "Traders"' third season, CanWest would share Canadian broadcast rights with the government-owned Canadian Broadcasting Corp. The agreement was expected to boost the show's reach in Canada.
Shares of Atlantis were up 0.45 to 9.75 in afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on more than 3,000 shares.
